placement.position_note: PARTY-LINE FRONTAGE, DERIVED FROM THE COMMITTED PLAT (T-0077). This building does not stand where a northing in the recipe put it: it stands on the north face of blk_lake_clark, whose line and bearing are read from the block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json — the same committed geometry the lot grid and the corridor gate are derived from. Its front wall is set 0.80 m back from that lot line, the alignment the two frontage buildings already standing on this face use, and its east wall is fixed by the west wall of recon_1835_south_d5_016, which it shares a party line with. The bearing is the face's own, and this placement carries none of the jitter the parcel's interior rows carry, because a shared party wall is one wall and cannot wander. WHAT IS INVENTED IS STILL EVERYTHING THAT MATTERS: that a building stood here at all, which building it was, and that these particular units stood shoulder to shoulder. What the plate supports is the TREATMENT — a continuous storefront row on the town's principal street rather than detached cottages set back on grass — and the treatment is what this placement takes from it. Standing on a derived block face is not standing on a recovered lot.

siding_exposure_m.note: INVENTED WITHIN A STOCK SET, NOT DERIVED. No source states the exposed face of any Chicago building's siding. The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this roof wears 5.5 in — dealt in this building's own parcel recipe: drawn on this record's stable key from the stocks its household class may hang (5 in, 5.5 in or 6 in; T-1839, docs/LIBERTIES.md L352), then advanced within them so that no roof of the parcel standing within 60 m hangs the same course. It is NOT keyed to a construction season the way the named buildings' stocks are: this record's 1835-01-01 is the programme's count-unit convention and not a date anything was built, so keying to it would deal every anonymous roof in the town one stock. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention and the recipe half is recorded beside it, under `tools/siding_stock.py`.

persons.name: Junis.A.or J.R.Cary
persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Junis.A.or J.R.Cary 2' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 1 July 1835, column 5 — dated 1835-07-01. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

citations.citation: Chicago · July 1835: Building Inventory and Architectural Reconstruction Specification. Prepared for Kevin Haas, August 2026.
what_it_supplies: A 665-roof production target with independently reconcilable group, district, level, and construction totals.
Thirty-five architectural family definitions with dimensional and massing bands.
District character, spacing, variation, finish, and chronology constraints for a July 1835 reconstruction.
A required distinction between named documentary landmarks and anonymous inferred infill.
what_it_does_not_supply: A surviving July 1835 building census or parcel-by-parcel roof register.
Exact locations, dimensions, appearance, occupants, or construction dates for anonymous roofs.
Authority to replace stronger building-specific evidence already represented in the dataset.

fabric_basis.words: silvered clapboard on a balloon frame, 12-over-12 sash of 6 × 8 in glass, plain corner boards and a stoop, under a weathered roof — a two-room frame cottage, a year old (rule F-T: a tradesman's by its type)

frontage.why: T-0077, the owner's ask of 2026-08-18 on the Tremont House street scene: "there should be more and denser buildings. this is important." He sent the plate of this corner — a continuous two-storey storefront row, shoulder to shoulder on shared party lines — beside a screenshot of this same corner in the render, where the Tremont stands alone on open grass. Four of this row's anonymous roofs stood in the Clark-Dearborn block SEVENTEEN TO TWENTY-FOUR METRES behind the Lake Street frontage, each nudged off the line by its own jitter, which is the shape of a distribution and not of a street. They now stand ON the frontage: the line, its bearing and the corner they pack back from are read from the committed block boundary in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json, and this file authors no coordinate for any of them. The 0.80 m setback is not a measurement — it is the line the two frontage buildings ALREADY standing on this face (inf_bakery_lake and inf_butcher_market) use, adopted so the street wall is one wall rather than three. No roof is added, moved out of its block, renamed or re-dimensioned: the parcel still deals 40 principal and 8 ancillary, and every id and band is the one it was.
